holidays.name: Peculiar People Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the odd ducks, eccentrics and one-of-a-kind characters in your life. It's also a day to admit that you might be one of them. Embrace your quirks, and give your most unconventional friends and relatives a high-five.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on quirky-holiday calendars as a salute to individuality and non-conformity.
holidays.funFact: The word 'peculiar' comes from the Latin 'peculiaris', meaning 'of one's own property'. So being peculiar literally means being uniquely your own.

holidays.name: National Oysters Rockefeller Day
holidays.description: A toast to the decadent baked-oyster dish. Oysters on the half shell are topped with a rich green blend of herbs and greens, butter and breadcrumbs, then broiled until bubbly. Put on your fanciest bib and slurp away.
holidays.origin: The dish was created in 1899 at Antoine's Restaurant in New Orleans by Jules Alciatore. He needed a substitute for escargot, which was in short supply. The rich green sauce earned it a name that nodded to oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller.
holidays.funFact: Antoine's has kept the exact recipe a closely guarded secret for over a century. It has served millions of orders of the dish.

holidays.name: National Bittersweet Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day for people who like their chocolate a little more grown-up. Bittersweet chocolate is deep, intense and less sugary than milk chocolate. Nibble it plain, melt it into desserts, or pair it with coffee or red wine.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is part of the winter lineup of chocolate-themed celebrations.
holidays.funFact: In the U.S., bittersweet chocolate must contain at least 35 percent cacao. Many bars go much higher, up to 70 percent or more.
